d: THE PROPHETIC HETERONYM, ROLE AND GENDER CARRIED. 'A heteronym of the writer Lee Sharks' stated in the opening; 'described explicitly as a female heteronym of Lee Sharks, with the role of prophetic overflow or political/prophetic voice'; Epistle to the Human Diaspora dated to 2015 circulation; the ASW introduction credited WITH the correction that the book is primarily Fraction's; the apostolic register quoted ('apostle of Jack Feist,' 'co-laborer of Lee Sharks'). The layer reads the persona as 'deliberately constructed as part of' the system — the fold cutting at exactly that recognition.

transcript: If you mean Damascus Dancings, the writer/poetic persona associated with the Crimson Hexagon project, the evidence points to her being a heteronym of the writer Lee Sharks, rather than a separate independently documented person. Dancings is described explicitly as a female heteronym of Lee Sharks, with the role of 'prophetic overflow' or political/prophetic voice. [Medium +1] Her principal identified work is Epistle to the Human Diaspora, originally circulating around 2015. [Medium +1] She is also credited with an introduction to Autonomous Semantic Warfare (2026), although that book is primarily by Rex Fraction. [Zenodo +1] The Dancings persona is presented in religious/apostolic language—'apostle of Jack Feist' and 'co-laborer of Lee Sharks'—and appears to be deliberately constructed as part of [fold]
